title: Domain of a Polynomial Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Without using a calculator, state the natural domain of the polynomial function f(x)=3x^2-2x+1: for which real inputs x does the formula produce a real output?

steps.title: List the Usual Domain Restrictions
steps.explanation: A formula can lose real inputs only through an even root of a negative number, division by zero, or a logarithm of a non-positive quantity.
steps.why: These are exactly the operations that are not defined for every real number.

steps.title: Inspect the Given Formula
steps.explanation: The expression is a polynomial: it only squares, multiplies by constants, and adds numbers, so every real x can be plugged in safely.
steps.why: Polynomials involve no roots, denominators, or logs, so no input is excluded.

steps.title: State the Domain
steps.explanation: Since no restriction applies, the natural domain is the entire real line.
steps.why: Every real input yields a real output, which is precisely the definition of domain equal to all reals.
